# kg_viewer

```{r setup}
#| include: false
library(DBI)
library(RSQLite)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(terra)
library(rnaturalearth)

q <- function(sql, params = NULL) {
  con <- dbConnect(SQLite(), "kg_climate.db", flags = SQLITE_RO)
  on.exit(dbDisconnect(con))
  dbGetQuery(con, sql, params = params)
}
build   <- with(q("SELECT * FROM buildInfo"), setNames(value, key))
legend  <- q("SELECT * FROM kgLegend ORDER BY kgValue")
kg_cols <- setNames(legend$hex, legend$kgCode)
species <- q("SELECT * FROM species")

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
            theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), plot.title.position = "plot",
                  plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA)))
```

**Can this pest live in Norway's climate?** `kg_viewer` answers the first part
of that question from evidence. It takes where a plant pest has been
recorded (GBIF), finds the Köppen-Geiger climate classes of those records,
and measures how much of Norway lies in the same classes, today and under a
warmer 2041–2070.

It produces background evidence for climate-suitability (EST1) judgements in
pest risk ranking. It is not a species distribution model.

**Live app:** <https://danielapp.shinyapps.io/kg-viewer/> ·
**Full method:** [`vignettes/kg_viewer.qmd`](vignettes/kg_viewer.qmd)

> Status: draft. All thresholds are judgement values and are stored with the
> data in `buildInfo`.

## A quick tour

Everything the app shows comes from one SQLite file, `kg_climate.db`. The
current build (`r substr(build[["buildDate"]], 1, 10)`) holds
`r nrow(species)` species and
`r format(sum(species$nCells), big.mark = ",")` cleaned 1 km occurrence cells.

```r
library(DBI)
con <- dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), "kg_climate.db", flags = RSQLite::SQLITE_RO)
```

### 1. Norway has a climate profile

Norway is measured by area, excluding the alpine and polar classes
(`r build[["excludedKg"]]`) where plant pests do not establish. Today it is
mostly cold-summer boreal **Dfc**. By 2041–2070 under SSP5-8.5, warm-summer
**Dfb** and oceanic **Cfb** take much of that ground.

```{r norway}
#| fig-height: 3
no <- bind_rows(
  q("SELECT * FROM kgNorway")       |> mutate(period = "1991–2020"),
  q("SELECT * FROM kgNorwayFuture") |> mutate(period = "2041–2070 SSP5-8.5")
) |>
  filter(proportion > 0.001) |>
  mutate(kgCode = reorder(kgCode, -proportion, max))

ggplot(no, aes(kgCode, proportion, fill = kgCode, alpha = period)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(0.8), width = 0.75, colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_text(aes(label = scales::percent(proportion, 1)),
            position = position_dodge(0.8), vjust = -0.3, size = 3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = kg_cols, guide = "none") +
  scale_alpha_manual(values = c(1, 0.45), name = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, expand = expansion(c(0, 0.12))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = "Share of non-alpine Norway per Köppen-Geiger class") +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

All classes, with area. Shares are of non-alpine mainland Norway, and classes
under 0.1 % are left out of the chart above.

```{r norway-table}
norway <- q("
  SELECT l.kgCode AS Class, l.kgLabel AS Climate,
         n.areaKm2 AS km2_now, n.proportion AS pct_now,
         f.areaKm2 AS km2_future, f.proportion AS pct_future
  FROM kgLegend l
  LEFT JOIN kgNorway n USING (kgCode)
  LEFT JOIN kgNorwayFuture f USING (kgCode)
  WHERE n.kgCode IS NOT NULL OR f.kgCode IS NOT NULL
  ORDER BY COALESCE(n.areaKm2, 0) DESC") |>
  mutate(across(starts_with(c("km2", "pct")), ~ coalesce(.x, 0)))

km2 <- function(x) format(round(x), big.mark = ",")
pct <- function(x) sprintf("%.2f %%", 100 * x)

norway |>
  add_row(Class = "**Total**", Climate = "",
          km2_now = sum(norway$km2_now), pct_now = 1,
          km2_future = sum(norway$km2_future), pct_future = 1) |>
  transmute(Class, Climate,
            `km² 1991–2020` = km2(km2_now), `% 1991–2020` = pct(pct_now),
            `km² 2041–2070` = km2(km2_future), `% 2041–2070` = pct(pct_future),
            `Change (pp)` = if_else(Class == "**Total**", "",
                                    sub("^[-+](0\\.00)$", "\\1",
                                        sprintf("%+.2f", 100 * (pct_future - pct_now))))) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "llrrrrr")
```

The non-alpine area differs between the periods (the total row) because
the alpine classes (ET, EF) shrink as the climate warms, and that land joins the
classes counted here.

### 2. A pest occupies some climate classes

Take the moth *Lymantria mathura* (`LYMAMA`). Its GBIF
records are cleaned and thinned to one per 1 km cell, and each cell gets
its climate class. The view `occupiedKgClasses` keeps the classes that pass
the occupancy rule: at least `r build[["occMinCells"]]` cells **and** at least
`r 100 * as.numeric(build[["occMinShare"]])` % of the species' cells. Single
stray or mislabelled records cannot add a class.

```{r classes}
classes <- q("
  SELECT p.kgCode, l.kgLabel, p.nCells,
         o.kgCode IS NOT NULL AS occupied
  FROM pestKgClasses p
  JOIN kgLegend l USING (kgCode)
  LEFT JOIN occupiedKgClasses o USING (eppoCode, kgCode)
  WHERE p.eppoCode = 'LYMAMA'
  ORDER BY p.nCells DESC")
classes
```

On the map, the shading shows the occupied classes. Filled points lie in them
and hollow points fall below the rule.

```{r map}
#| fig-height: 4.2
occ_codes <- classes$kgCode[classes$occupied == 1]
pts <- q("SELECT lon, lat, kgCode FROM occurrences WHERE eppoCode = 'LYMAMA'") |>
  mutate(status = if_else(kgCode %in% occ_codes, "occupied class", "below rule"))

kg_df <- rast("koppen_geiger_0p1.tif") |>
  crop(ext(60, 180, 0, 75)) |>
  as.data.frame(xy = TRUE) |>
  setNames(c("x", "y", "kgValue")) |>
  left_join(select(legend, kgValue, kgCode), by = "kgValue") |>
  filter(kgCode %in% occ_codes)
world <- ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf")

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = world, fill = "grey92", colour = NA) +
  geom_raster(data = kg_df, aes(x, y, fill = kgCode), alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_sf(data = world, fill = NA, colour = "grey45", linewidth = 0.1) +
  geom_point(data = pts, aes(lon, lat, shape = status), fill = "red", size = 1.2, stroke = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = kg_cols, name = NULL) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("occupied class" = 21, "below rule" = 1), name = NULL) +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(60, 180), ylim = c(0, 75), expand = FALSE) +
  labs(title = expression(italic("Lymantria mathura") ~ "in its occupied climate classes"),
       x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "right")
```

### 3. The overlap is the evidence

The overlap with Norway is the share of non-alpine Norway that lies in the
occupied classes:

```{r overlap}
q("SELECT o.kgCode,
          ROUND(n.proportion * 100, 1) AS pctNorway,
          ROUND(f.proportion * 100, 1) AS pctNorway2041_2070
   FROM occupiedKgClasses o
   LEFT JOIN kgNorway n USING (kgCode)
   LEFT JOIN kgNorwayFuture f USING (kgCode)
   WHERE o.eppoCode = 'LYMAMA' AND (n.proportion > 0 OR f.proportion > 0)")
```

For *L. mathura* that is about a quarter of Norway today, rising to over 40 %
by mid-century. It occupies Dfb and Cfb, and its 3 cells in Dfc fall below the
rule.

### 4. The same overlap for every species

```{r all}
#| fig-height: 3.6
overlap <- q("
  SELECT s.eppoCode, s.uncertainty,
    COALESCE((SELECT SUM(n.proportion) FROM occupiedKgClasses o JOIN kgNorway n
              USING (kgCode) WHERE o.eppoCode = s.eppoCode), 0) AS now,
    COALESCE((SELECT SUM(f.proportion) FROM occupiedKgClasses o JOIN kgNorwayFuture f
              USING (kgCode) WHERE o.eppoCode = s.eppoCode), 0) AS future,
    (SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(kgCode, '+') FROM (SELECT kgCode FROM occupiedKgClasses o
       WHERE o.eppoCode = s.eppoCode AND kgCode IN ('Dfc', 'Dfb', 'Cfb')
       ORDER BY kgCode DESC)) AS shared
  FROM species s") |>
  mutate(uncertainty = factor(uncertainty, c("low", "medium", "high")),
         shared = coalesce(shared, "none of these"),
         label  = sprintf("%s:  %s → %s", shared,
                          scales::percent(now, 1), scales::percent(future, 1)))

# Overlap is a sum of a few class shares, so species fall into a few groups
ggplot(overlap, aes(y = reorder(label, now), fill = uncertainty)) +
  geom_bar(width = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(low = "#1b7837", medium = "#e08214", high = "#b2182b"),
                    name = "Uncertainty") +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(c(0, 0.05))) +
  labs(x = "Number of species", y = NULL,
       title = "Overlap with Norway, 1991–2020 → 2041–2070, all species",
       subtitle = "Grouped by which of Norway's main classes they occupy") +
  theme(legend.position = "top", panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```

Because the overlap adds up shares of only a few classes, the species fall
into a handful of groups. A few occupy Dfc and already overlap with most of
Norway. A large group lives in Dfb and/or Cfb and gains ground as Norway
warms. Many sit at 0 % in both periods, restricted to climates that Norway
does not have. A few share only marginal classes such as Cfc, which nearly
vanish by 2041–2070.

### 5. How sure is the class list?

A pest with 30 records may occupy classes nobody has sampled yet. The build
redraws `r build[["stabRuns"]]` random halves of each species' cells and
checks whether the occupied classes found in Norway stay the same. The
resulting `uncertainty` column (low / medium / high) combines that stability
with the number of cells, and belongs next to the overlap in any assessment
text.

```{r unc}
q("SELECT uncertainty, COUNT(*) AS species FROM species GROUP BY uncertainty")
```

Other columns of `species` add supporting evidence: cells already in Norway or
the Nordic countries, a robust poleward edge (`lat95`), whether a cold-summer
boreal class is occupied, and the share of records since 2000.

## Running it

```r
install.packages(c("shiny", "bslib", "leaflet", "DT", "terra", "png", "DBI",
                   "RSQLite", "dplyr", "rnaturalearth", "rnaturalearthdata",
                   "xfun", "htmltools"))
shiny::runApp(".")                                   # from the repository root
rsconnect::deployApp(".", appName = "kg-viewer")     # update the live app
```

The app needs no web map tiles; it draws country outlines itself. It builds
its map images from a 1-byte class index instead of calling
`leaflet::addRasterImage()`, which keeps memory well under shinyapps.io's 1 GB.

## Rebuilding the data

`kg_db.R` builds `kg_climate.db`. You also need `rgbif`, `CoordinateCleaner`
and `readxl`, plus two inputs that are not in this repository:

- **The species list.** An Excel sheet with `eppocode`, `fullname`,
  `kingdom` and `batch`. Set `SPECIES_FILE` to its path.
- **The 1 km Köppen-Geiger rasters** from <https://www.gloh2o.org/koppen/>,
  1991–2020 and 2041–2070/ssp585. Set `KG_DIR` to their folder.

`OUT_DB` and `GBIF_CACHE_DIR` still point to `./scripts/kg_viewer/` from this
app's original project. Set both to `.` here. Downloads are cached per species
in `gbif_cache/`, so a rebuild with new thresholds needs no network access.

In outline, the build:

1. matches each species to the GBIF backbone;
2. downloads records in latitude bands, which avoids GBIF's slow deep paging;
3. drops fossil specimens, living specimens and managed records, and records
   with more than 10 km uncertainty, then runs CoordinateCleaner tests;
4. thins the records to one per 1 km cell and looks up each cell's climate
   class;
5. computes overlap, stability and the supporting indicators.

## Files and tables

| File | |
|---|---|
| `app.R` | Shiny app (reads `kg_climate.db` read-only) |
| `kg_db.R` | Database build |
| `kg_climate.db` | The data |
| `koppen_geiger_*_0p1.tif` | Beck et al. 2023 maps at 0.1°, for map shading |
| `gbif_cache/` | Raw GBIF records per species |
| `vignettes/` | Method vignette with literature, limitations and references |
| `README.qmd` | Source of this page; render with `quarto render README.qmd` |

| Table | |
|---|---|
| `species` | Per species: GBIF match, counts, Nordic/European presence, `lat95`, stability, `uncertainty` |
| `occurrences` | Cleaned cells with lon/lat, climate class and years |
| `pestKgClasses` | Cells per species × class (raw, unthresholded) |
| `occupiedKgClasses` | *View*: the classes passing the occupancy rule |
| `kgNorway`, `kgNorwayFuture` | Norway's km² and share per class |
| `kgLegend`, `buildInfo` | Class names and colours; every setting used in the build |
